approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a bidirectional masked denoiser on unlabeled molecular fragment sequences and freezes its neural weights. For each objective it ranks previously scored whole molecules, samples high-ranked ones as contexts, and replaces one fragment with a variable-length masked span. The model fills that span while retaining the surrounding fragments and attachment labels. Valid, connected, canonical new molecules are submitted in generation order; accepted scores update the archive and therefore the contexts used next. Parallel denoising usually produces more usable completions than fit in the announced batch, and the Parent discards that surplus.
approach.novelty: Add one mechanism: posterior-sampling selection among the fresh completions already produced by the Parent. A molecular-fingerprint Gaussian process fitted only to accepted scores represents uncertain objective values, and joint posterior draws select distinct completions for the batch. This is the first selector Child in this lineage; its only supplied sibling is the unmodified remasking root. The related graph-evolution experiment made a much larger offspring pool. Here the new selector uses the natural surplus of the existing denoising calls, so the experiment asks whether better use of those alternatives changes the search's best outcomes.

hypothesis: Replace generation-order submission with distinct maximizers of independent joint posterior function draws from an accepted-only, task-local Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process over the Parent's existing fresh surplus SAFE fragment completions.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection replicated: uncertainty redirected 68% of eligible choices, while final scores varied across seeds
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now rules out activation being peculiar to the first seed: accepted-only posterior updates, use of cross-candidate covariance, and uncertainty-driven changes to actual submissions all persisted across different prepared denoisers and search trajectories. The natural surplus was sufficient for selection in 285 of 290 new batches without increasing the inherited generation width or generating beyond the first sufficient call. Correct activation still leaves efficacy unresolved. Chronological GP prediction error beat the archive-mean predictor in nine of ten new task runs, but lost on seed-2 sitagliptin (RMSE 0.06228 versus 0.05839). The lower-scoring second replica had lower pooled prediction error and more completions beating their contexts than the first; neither diagnostic alone establishes better final best scores. Unsubmitted alternatives have no oracle labels, and there are no matched generation-order or greedy-mean control runs here. The molecular assessment further limits what the selector can accomplish: it reallocates calls among mostly related aromatic analogue families and inherits gaps in scaffold coverage, stereochemical specification and chemical plausibility. High scores and score ties across chemically different products do not by themselves show that reactive or questionable structures have been avoided. A matched selector ablation with the same prepared prior, together with inspection of the high-scoring chemistry, would separate the value of correlated uncertainty from prior quality and score permissiveness.
finding_summary.results: Both new replicas executed accepted-only GP conditioning and full-covariance posterior selection. Across their ten task runs, all 280 nonterminal feedback probes changed the posterior mean and variance on the same previously submitted molecules. Every one of 2,900 choices replayed as the maximum of its logged joint draw over the remaining pool. Selection changed the submitted generation-order set in 284 of 285 batches with surplus completions, replacing 1,304 prefix entries. Uncertainty changed 1,939 of 2,850 eligible choices (68.04%) relative to the posterior-mean maximizer of the identical remaining pool. The five batches without surplus were excluded from that uncertainty denominator; there were no numerical fallbacks, fingerprint collisions or exact choice ties. The same mechanism was already active in the supplied seed-0 baseline, where uncertainty changed 1,019 of 1,450 choices (70.28%). These are replications of activation, not new algorithm changes. The new macro scores were 0.50778 and 0.47068, alongside the original 0.50903. The three-seed mean was 0.49583 with population standard deviation 0.01779. Task means were 0.41036 for zaleplon, 0.59284 for scaffold hopping, 0.96337 for DRD2 docking, 0.20040 for median similarity and 0.31218 for sitagliptin. All tasks completed 300 oracle evaluations. The supplied comparison runs are the same selector on different seeds, so they do not establish a replicated score improvement over generation-order submission.

molecular.headline: Dense aromatic analogue families, with useful amines but repeated radical ions, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories cover seeds 1 and 2 of this Algorithm Node, with seed 0 of the same node as the comparison baseline. All five tasks are covered, each with 580 optimizer proposals among 600 evaluated records. The output contains recognizable indole carboxamides, benzothiazoles, pyrazoline thioureas, fused pyrimidinediones, arylpiperazines and more unusual cyclic polyamines. Related scaffolds recur with halogen, alkoxy, carbonyl and linker substitutions. Diversity is moderate across the combined output but much narrower within individual high-scoring families; distinct SMILES often represent close analogues. Every task has ring_closure_rate 1.0, and aromatic-atom indicator rates range from 0.9741 to 1.0. These indicate presence of ring digits and aromatic atoms, not that every ring is aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.4 to 62.1, and the trajectories include both ordinary medicinal-sized frameworks and very long appended chains or macrocycles. The conventional cores support moderate drug-likeness, but overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because peripheral changes repeatedly introduce hydroperoxides, bare radical ions, unusual sulfur valence patterns and strained unsaturated rings. A syntactically accepted structure is not evidence of an isolable closed-shell compound. All stereocentre indicator rates are 0.0 despite visibly stereogenic aminals, branched arylalkyl chains and substituted saturated rings. The output therefore supplies substantial ring and aromatic chemistry while leaving chemical form, configuration and the stability of appended functionality unresolved. Several exact score ties between chemically different substituents make these omissions particularly visible.

per_task.generated_character: The main families are multiply substituted benzothiazoles with an anilinomethyl arm, methoxy/methylthio/acetyl substituents, and dimethoxyindole carboxamides or indole–oxadiazole combinations. A smaller acetyl-substituted pyrazoline thiourea is the best molecule. These are mostly medium-sized, ring-rich frameworks with plausible synthetic building blocks. Mean SMILES length is 45.4; ring and aromatic indicators are both 1.0, and halogen_rate is 0.7948. The low-scoring tail includes highly extended bridged-ring appendages and unusual boron or sulfur chemistry.
liabilities: The best molecule retains a thiourea, and the benzothiazole family frequently carries a thioether; their chemical reactivity and oxidation-state stability require assessment independent of the score.

The unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur oxide linkage and the borane are chemically less straightforward than the conventional heteroaryl cores. Very large, densely connected ring appendages also create substantial synthetic complexity.
missing_features: Chemically controlled changes to the central heterocycle, linker and carbonyl pattern remain more informative than the repeated terminal F/Cl/Br substitutions that share a score; the high group is concentrated in close benzothiazole analogues.
The stereogenic carbon in the best substituted pyrazoline is unspecified. The trajectories do not show whether configuration affects this objective.
No uniquely missing target motif is established; the visible evidence favors a moderate-sized aromatic/polar arrangement already present in several different families.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The acetyl pyrazoline thiourea scores 0.41237650262954906, compared with 0.1501184006136499 for the initial hydroxyphenyl-substituted pyrazoline thiourea. This supports a favorable change in size and substituent balance within that broad family, without isolating a single causal property. The seed-0 best, another pyrazoline thiourea with an aldehyde-containing arm, scored 0.4443186615775074. The new benzothiazole methylthio series reaches 0.404945686740228 with F, Cl or Br on the terminal phenyl, giving exactly the same recorded score for those substitutions. The corresponding dimethoxy variants score 0.38519625255195356, while the diacetyl/methylthio example scores 0.4064265251651748. These local comparisons implicate the central substitution pattern more than terminal halogen identity. The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; late indole–oxadiazole chemistry remains moderate at 0.2853198676066052. A massively extended indole derivative scores 1.7016180040499976e-35 and the small phenyl/hydroxymethyl borane scores 8.713153723578382e-09. The median is 0.196853, so neither indiscriminate extension nor drastic truncation is supported.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high scorers largely retain a fused N-methyl pyrimidinedione connected to a substituted aryl group and a pyridyl or phenyl partner through a cyanamide-bearing aminal or N,O-acetal. Some carry long conjugated ketone side chains. Seed 2 also explores oxygen-rich medium-ring systems bearing aminomethyl heteroaryl and oxazole-like groups. These are larger and more elaborated than the simplest initial molecules: mean SMILES length is 62.1, with ring and aromatic indicators both 1.0 and halogen_rate 0.6776. The core heterocycles are recognizable, but several linkers and substituents make isolation and stability questionable.
liabilities: Cyanamide-bearing aminal and N,O-acetal connections raise hydrolytic-stability and chemical-form questions.
High-scoring examples encode terminal nitrogen radical anions; other examples contain extended conjugated ketones or an O–S(=O)2–S group ending in a very small unsaturated ring.
A late indole derivative contains a nitrosoalkyl substituent. These functionalities warrant specific chemical assessment, not an assumption of ordinary screening-library behavior.
missing_features: Stable, closed-shell alternatives to the recurrent cyanamide aminals, N,O-acetals and exotic appended fragments are insufficiently demonstrated around the same favorable aryl/heteroaryl arrangement.
The aminal stereocentre and geometries of conjugated unsaturated side chains are unspecified. Their effects cannot be inferred from the score ties.
A unique missing decoration is not identifiable from the available scalar scores; additional size or functional-group complexity is often tolerated without establishing a better chemical candidate.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cyanamide-bearing aminal linking a pyridyl group to the aryl/fused-dione system scores 0.5974361625142148, above the initial fused-dione ester at 0.548381482770623. The seed-0 best, a different fused azaarene with an aminomethyl aryl arm and an ether chain, scored 0.5937687401188465. Both favor connected heteroaromatic/polar architectures, without specifying a unique scaffold. A particularly revealing series has the identical score 0.5900771267411073 for an N-methyl dione and variants with terminal bare [N-] groups. Graph interpretation of those terminal groups includes an unpaired electron; they are radical anions rather than ordinary protonation variants. The score therefore does not distinguish a conventional member of this series from those chemically problematic appendages. The worst proposal at 0.3047122074636306 introduces a sulfone joined to a large unsaturated carbocycle. Other digest low proposals lie around 0.527–0.531 and have simpler ester/carbonyl substitution or short indole amide arms. The median is 0.567667. A final medium-ring molecule with an O–S(=O)2–S linkage still scores 0.5873236733518856, again separating favorable numerical features from demonstrated chemical robustness.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high group is a tightly related arylpiperazine family: an exposed aliphatic piperazine nitrogen connects through a branched alkyl chain to a second substituted aromatic ring. Methoxy, phenol and multiple F/Cl/I substitutions dominate. Seed 2 instead repeatedly combines substituted pyrrolidines and secondary amines with arylalkyl, biaryl or fused aromatic groups; some retain carboxylic acid or amide side chains. The recognizable amine/aryl frameworks are generally makeable, although unusual halogenated N-substituents occur. Mean SMILES length is 58.0, ring_closure_rate is 1.0, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9828 and halogen_rate is 0.9845.
liabilities: Near-universal halogenation adds chemical mass and extensive aromatic substitution; neither the near-unity scores nor the exact ties establish improved experimental binding or acceptable physicochemical properties.
Some late N-substituents place fluorine, hydroxy or amino groups on the same carbon attached to ring nitrogen. The final N–C(O)(F)F group in particular requires chemical-form and stability scrutiny.
missing_features: Configurations are unspecified at the branched arylalkyl stereocentre and the substituted pyrrolidine/side-chain centres, even within the repeatedly high-scoring families.

Less heavily halogenated, chemically conservative alternatives retaining the favorable amine/aryl spacing are poorly represented; the observed score ties do not establish a requirement for iodine or any exact halogen pattern.
The trajectories do not provide a basis for naming an additional obligatory target interaction beyond the observed exposed-amine and aromatic arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched arylalkyl/arylpiperazine reaches 0.9999999869310162. The same score is recorded after replacing F with Cl on one ring, replacing iodine with chlorine, or changing a chlorine on the other ring to fluorine. The observed favorable arrangement is therefore clearer than any specific required halogen. The seed-0 best at 0.9640302775641455 was an arylcyclopropyl aminoalcohol linked to an N-substituted pyrrolidine, also retaining exposed aliphatic amines. The initial sulfonylated-pyrrolidine/amide/acid framework scores 0.01904115112334333; close early relatives remain low. A late molecule that preserves the branched arylalkyl region but replaces the piperazine region with a carbonyl-containing N-heterocycle and sulfone scores 0.007091365028079139. The contrast supports the importance of amine availability and its surrounding geometry, rather than nitrogen content alone. The median is 0.647607, and late seed-2 amine-containing structures score 0.7853743688684828 to 0.8786262267384644 in the cited examples. Acid-containing molecules can therefore remain favorable when the broader amine/aryl arrangement is retained.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 concentrates on aryl esters or alpha-ketoesters joined through a substituted ethyl unit to indole or benzodioxole and a methylated seven-membered triaza ring. That saturated ring has an adjacent N–N bond at its closure; it should not be described as an ordinary piperazine. Aldehyde, fluoro/chloro and occasional unusual sulfur substitutions diversify this family. Seed 1 stays mainly around aryl-substituted fused pyrimidinediones with small saturated-ring or ether decorations. Mean SMILES length is 60.8, with ring and aromatic indicators both 1.0. The combined population contains reasonable aromatic building blocks but chemically more complicated polyamines and occasional very large ring expansions.
liabilities: An aldehyde is present in the best molecule, and several neighbors carry alpha-ketoesters; their reactivity is a separate issue from the small differences in score.
The cyclic polyamine contains an N–N bond, while a later variant adds an N–O bond. Protonation, oxidation and chemical stability should not be assumed from the neutral SMILES.
A relatively high-scoring example includes an unusual sulfur oxide/ylide-like connection to a small ring; the low tail also contains hydrogen-bearing sulfur structures and enormous ring expansions.
missing_features: Stereochemical specification of the carbon connecting the aryl group, linker and cyclic polyamine is absent across the favorable series.
Alternative stable saturated linkers or nitrogen-ring arrangements that preserve the favorable aromatic spacing are insufficiently demonstrated outside the recurrent triaza-ring family.

The observed indole/benzodioxole contrast supports a local chemical preference, but it does not identify a uniquely missing target scaffold or prove that further aldehyde/carbonyl addition would help.

Its closely related indole counterpart scores 0.20125723423387007, making replacement of the fused heteroaromatic unit a more interpretable local contrast than a generic increase in ring content. transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains terminal nitrogen radical-anion variants with exactly the same score, 0.5900771267411073, as a conventional N-methyl relative. It also shows hydroperoxides, an N–Br heterocycle, a bare carbon cation with radical valence, and unusual hydrogen-bearing or multiply bonded sulfur linkages. Some of these remain among comparatively high-scoring or late proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve closed-shell, chemically interpretable molecular forms during otherwise local changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemistry-aware control of hydrogen count, valence, charge and radical state, and stable alternatives to reactive linkages within the same scaffold families. Keep chemical form distinct from numerical score: observed objective values alone do not reject these changes. Do not equate every ordinary ionizable group with the bare radical-ion fragments shown here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A benzothiazole series with F, Cl or Br shares score 0.404945686740228. Several differently halogenated arylpiperazines share 0.9999999869310162, and aryl ester/fused-dione positional variants share 0.343704064948769. The best groups repeatedly retain the same central ring and linker arrangements despite these peripheral changes.
transferable_gaps.gap: Repeated terminal substitutions produce distinct strings without demonstrating broader chemical capabilities around the favorable cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically conservative changes to central ring topology, linker connectivity and functional-group arrangement accessible while retaining useful portions of observed molecules. Let task-local feedback determine whether those changes matter; repeated halogen swaps should not be treated as evidence that broad chemical neighborhoods have been explored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 580 optimizer proposals. Digest high scorers contain a substituted pyrazoline carbon, a cyanamide-bearing aminal carbon, a branched arylalkyl carbon and a carbon joining aryl and cyclic-polyamine groups, all without specified configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic output is left unspecified even in densely sampled favorable analogue families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable specification and preservation of stereochemical identities where those centers exist, and compare them through current task-local observations. The files establish the omission but do not identify its implementation cause or prove that any particular objective distinguishes the stereoisomers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Task mean SMILES lengths range from 45.4 to 62.1 and maxima from 77 to 95. The digest worst examples include very long alkyl/acyl extensions, massive hydrocarbon macrocycles and densely connected bridged appendages. Compact neighboring cores can score favorably, whereas a large macrocycle scores 0.0 and long-chain examples reach 2.4700785835147185e-67 and 5.3678001758351103e-67.
transferable_gaps.gap: Controlled scaffold extension is missing at the boundary between useful substituent variation and excessive molecular growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded variation of chain length, ring size and appendage complexity around existing cores, using task-local feedback to set useful ranges. Preserve the option for legitimately larger structures while preventing uncontrolled growth from substituting for chemically meaningful exploration.

method_name: GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser
method_thesis: Anchor the method in GenMol's fragment-remasking mechanism: a bidirectional masked discrete diffusion model generates replacement fragments while retaining the surrounding molecular context. The anchor is described in [GenMol, Sections 4.1-4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.06158v3). For this benchmark adaptation, train a compact denoiser solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, then freeze it. Start each objective with a fresh archive of its supplied scored molecules. Select high-ranked observed whole molecules as contexts, replace a randomly chosen fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively sample the missing SAFE tokens, and decode the resulting complete molecule. Generate further completions until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. Accepted feedback updates context selection and allows improving completions to become future contexts. This root uses the remasking core with observed whole-molecule contexts; the paper's corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary initialization and fragment-attaching stage are not required. The corpus trains the denoiser and supplies unlabeled length statistics, never a molecule pool for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that contextual fragment replacement preserves useful structure while generating improving alternatives, raising the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Task-local selection can respond immediately to feedback without reward-dependent neural training, but useful conditional generation from the permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

applicability_conditions: Applies to task-local scalar maximization with accepted molecular scores and valid fresh completion surplus from an already functioning context-preserving denoiser. The Parent supplies that prerequisite on one screening replica; its score deviation of zero is not evidence of cross-seed stability.

Selection can exploit only alternatives produced by the unchanged single-fragment remasking process. This Child does not resolve inaccessible scaffolds, poor decoding, or objective optima outside those conditional neighborhoods. A batch with no surplus provides no submitted-set selection opportunity.

A Tanimoto GP assumes useful structure in the relationship between fingerprints and scores. Chronological prediction errors and kernel uncertainty may be poorly calibrated; the mechanism can execute while directing calls poorly. No labels for discarded completions exist, so same-pool counterfactual rankings establish decision changes, not counterfactual oracle gains.

The confirmed posterior-selector observation n-fc2c108a5253 supplies analogous single-seed feasibility evidence, not a settled transfer result for masked diffusion. Its worse parent-beating frequency is why this intent does not make increased average context-relative proposal quality an activation requirement. approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a bidirectional masked denoiser on unlabeled molecular fragment sequences and freezes its neural weights. For each objective it ranks previously scored whole molecules, samples high-ranked ones as contexts, and replaces one fragment with a variable-length masked span. The model fills that span while retaining the surrounding fragments and attachment labels. Valid, connected, canonical new molecules are submitted in generation order; accepted scores update the archive and therefore the contexts used next. Parallel denoising usually produces more usable completions than fit in the announced batch, and the Parent discards that surplus.
approach.novelty: Add one mechanism: posterior-sampling selection among the fresh completions already produced by the Parent. A molecular-fingerprint Gaussian process fitted only to accepted scores represents uncertain objective values, and joint posterior draws select distinct completions for the batch. This is the first selector Child in this lineage; its only supplied sibling is the unmodified remasking root. The related graph-evolution experiment made a much larger offspring pool. Here the new selector uses the natural surplus of the existing denoising calls, so the experiment asks whether better use of those alternatives changes the search's best outcomes.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection changed every batch and lifted the single-seed macro score to 0.509
finding_summary.insights:
The existing completion surplus was sufficient to redirect search without enlarging generation or changing the frozen denoiser. Uncertainty affected which molecules reached evaluation: 138 of 145 selected sets differed from the ten highest posterior means. Its contribution to the score gain remains open because those unsubmitted alternatives have no oracle labels and there is no greedy-mean ablation.

Better final best scores did not require better average proposals relative to their generating contexts. The context-beating count fell from 273 to 242 out of 1,450, and mean completion-minus-context score worsened from −0.069910 to −0.079941. The GP predicted accepted scores more accurately than the current archive-mean baseline on every objective, yet median_2 still lost final score. Prediction accuracy and frequent small improvements therefore do not settle whether search finds the best rare products. The chemistry assessment places much of the successful output within recurring scaffold families and identifies reactive or strained attachments and unspecified stereochemistry. The score gains leave those coverage and chemical-quality limitations unresolved. This single paired seed establishes execution and an observed gain; it does not establish reliability across seeds.

molecular_assessment.headline: Aromatic scaffold families with useful free-amine chemistry, but reactive attachments, strained cores and no specified stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Assessment of the supplied seed-0 trajectories for n-07478bd19615 against Parent n-de3f755cf329. All five tasks are covered; each digest contains 300 observed molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. These are mostly medium-sized to bulky, branched, ring-rich molecules, with distinct diaryl pyrazoline-thiourea, oxygen-rich benzimidazole/benzocyclopropene, biaryl aminopyrrolidine and fused pyrrolopyrimidinedione families. The proposal ring_closure_rate is 1.0 on every task, aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.9828 to 1.0, and mean SMILES length ranges from 42.7 to 65.0. These are text counters, not atom fractions, molecular weights or perceived ring counts. Aromatic character is abundant; missing rings are not the problem. Across tasks there is moderate structural variety, but each high-scoring region is much narrower than canonical uniqueness suggests. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry groups coexist with aldehydes, unusual halogenated amine attachments, strained fused small rings and reactive nitrogen substitutions. Apparent makeability is therefore mixed. All stereocentre_rate counters are 0.0 despite structures with stereogenic sites. Scores below are the supplied observations, not new calculations of objective values. Structure-score associations do not establish a hidden reference pharmacophore, synthetic route or biological activity.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring molecules are compact diaryl pyrazolines: a partly saturated nitrogen-containing ring bearing phenyl groups and an N-linked thiourea. The best structures attach a short aldehyde-containing chain to the other thiourea nitrogen; some also contain an amide, a phenol or an aryl halogen. A separate trimethoxy indole-carboxanilide family appears among the initial and generated structures. The optimizer mean SMILES length is 42.7; every proposal has ring-closure and aromatic text, and halogen_rate is 0.5. The diaryl heterocyclic cores look synthetically recognizable, but the complete functional-group combinations need more scrutiny than the core alone.
liabilities: The leading aldehydes are electrophilic and potentially oxidation-sensitive; thiourea and N-acylthiourea functionality adds further chemical-handling questions. These are potential liabilities, not measured toxicity or proof that the molecules cannot be made.
The low-scoring organoboron fragment and enlarged charged unsaturated structures show that formally accepted molecular identities can still be unusual synthetic targets.
missing_features: Many low-scoring completions lose the intact diaryl placement or overload it with additional ring material. Controlled replacement that retains the favorable size and polar-group arrangement is missing from those products.

The best excerpt does not demonstrate an alternative stable linker/core family matching these scores without the aldehyde-thiourea combination. The trajectories do not establish which absent heterocycle, if any, the objective specifically needs.
Configuration is unspecified at the substituted pyrazoline carbon; the record contains no evidence of a preferred stereoisomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Initial evaluation 9, the indole carboxanilide, scores 0.3051048083696145; initial evaluation 3, the N-phenyl diaryl pyrazoline-thiourea, scores 0.1501184006136499. The best generated structure, evaluation 146, retains the diaryl pyrazoline-thiourea and adds an aldehyde-containing N-substituent and meta phenol, scoring 0.4443186615775074. Its para-phenol counterpart at evaluation 276 scores 0.4215873828756271. The meta Br, Cl and F aldehyde-amide analogues at evaluations 202, 212 and 232 all score 0.439920472922802, so those halogen substitutions do not separate their scores. Replacing an aryl group with a fluoromethyl group at evaluation 295 gives 0.04800098880856684; greatly enlarging that aryl substituent at evaluation 297 gives 0.0002895801120799731. The small organoboron product at evaluation 292 scores 2.1134099902378706e-08. This supports a compact, correctly substituted diaryl/polar-group arrangement within the observed neighborhood, rather than simply more aromatic mass. Parent evaluation 280 reached 0.4237289437603468 with the same broad pyrazoline-thiourea family but N-chloro and chloroketone functionality; the Child changes the peripheral chemistry without leaving that family.

per_task.generated_character: The Child produces fairly bulky, oxygen-rich aromatic compounds with alkoxy substituents and arylaminomethyl or carboxamide connections. Many high scorers contain a geminal dialkoxy carbon in a three-membered ring fused to benzene, a strained benzocyclopropene framework. Their appendages include fluorophenyl or fluoroisoxazolyl groups, benzodioxoles, benzodioxanes and furans. The highest-scoring structure instead has an N-aryl benzimidazole, an anilinomethyl group and an unsaturated alkoxy chain. Thus an alternative core is actually present. Mean SMILES length is 51.8; ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 1.0, and halogen_rate is 0.7931. The benzimidazole family is more conventional synthetically than the repeated gem-dialkoxy fused small-ring products.
liabilities: A benzene-fused three-membered ring with geminal oxygen substitution combines ring strain with potentially labile acetal chemistry; accepted SMILES do not establish preparative practicality or storage stability.

Evaluation 283 also contains a small unsaturated carbonyl ring and an enol ether while still scoring 0.5880981763334705. Such structures illustrate why high scores cannot substitute for chemistry review.
Extended aryl ether and unsaturated chains add conformational freedom and hydrophobic surface to already aromatic molecules; no solubility or metabolic measurements are supplied.
missing_features: The successful strained-core series lacks a demonstrated broad set of ordinary unstrained replacements preserving its favorable arylaminomethyl/oxygen substitution pattern. The benzimidazole products establish that changing the core is possible, so a total absence of scaffold variation would be an incorrect diagnosis.
Stereochemical assignments are absent for asymmetric gem-dialkoxy fused-ring products. No additional objective-specific missing pharmacophore can be justified from this narrow high-score band.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fluorophenyl indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 scores 0.5464020559680183. Its cyclobutylsulfonyl-decorated analogue at evaluation 13 scores 0.3011099962373009. A long-chain diynyl aromatic ester at evaluation 64 reaches only 0.5126742712294043. High structures preserve a compact arrangement of aromatic, ether and nitrogen connections: the benzocyclopropene example at evaluation 222 scores 0.5882678652856491, and the benzimidazole at evaluation 291 reaches 0.5937687401188465. The methoxy benzimidazole analogue at evaluation 262 scores 0.5837636981987656, showing a modest gain for that observed alkoxy-chain change, not a general rule favoring unlimited chain growth. The final fluorinated benzimidazole at evaluation 300 remains high at 0.5864175457417009. Parent evaluation 260 reached 0.5906837555165951 with an aryl/pyridyl fused-dione series. The Child therefore reaches similar observed values through different cores; the modest score separation cannot identify a uniquely required further scaffold change.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring family is a medium-to-large halogenated biaryl attached through a substituted cyclopropane and amino-bearing carbon to an aminomethyl pyrrolidine. It carries a free secondary amine and a tertiary cyclic amine, with alcohol, fluoromethyl or chloromethyl variants and small alkyl/haloalkyl groups on the ring nitrogen. These are mixed aromatic/aliphatic structures with substantially more three-dimensional carbon connectivity than the fused-dione families. Every proposal has ring-closure text, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9862, halogen_rate is 0.9793 and mean SMILES length is 56.3. The principal carbon skeleton and amine functionality are recognizable medicinal chemistry, although some peripheral attachments are questionable.

Frequent alpha-haloalkyl amine and chloromethyl attachments introduce potential reactivity concerns. The record does not determine protonation equilibria, and a low charged-SMILES rate does not mean these amines are uncharged in solution.
Multiple possible stereoisomers are unresolved; the reported objective values do not establish a particular stereoisomer, measured affinity or selectivity.
missing_features: Substituted cyclopropanes, the adjacent amino-bearing carbon and substituted pyrrolidines are emitted without defined stereochemistry. The generator does not demonstrate control over their relative or absolute configuration.

The best excerpt offers many peripheral substitutions on the same amine-to-biaryl topology, but little evidence of equally successful alternative arrangements of those features. A lack of basic amines would be the wrong diagnosis: this family already contains them.

per_task.generated_character: The products are comparatively bulky polyaromatic fused pyrrolopyrimidinediones with N-alkyl groups, aryl ethers and ester or amide side chains. The high-scoring examples attach indole or naphthalene-based groups, sometimes with cyclopropyl or cyclopentyl substitution. Evaluation 277 contains an N-chloro dione and still scores 0.19158901118370336. Evaluation 276 contains an N-attached nitrosomethyl group, rather than an ordinary stable alkyl substituent, and scores 0.19046508496409892.

Comparable changes in donor/acceptor placement without simply increasing aromatic bulk remain poorly demonstrated.

The best generated compound, evaluation 265, adds an indole-containing aromatic arrangement with bromoethoxyphenyl and N-cyclopentyl substitution and scores 0.1993252969257374. The quoted substituted pyrazolines, cyclopropane-linked amino compounds, substituted pyrrolidines and asymmetric gem-dialkoxy fused-ring products nevertheless contain sites where configuration can matter. The useful property envelope should be learned from the current accepted structures and scores, rather than imposed as universal growth, shrinkage or aromaticity rules.

Selection can exploit only alternatives produced by the unchanged single-fragment remasking process. All labeled state, fingerprints, posterior fits and pool contents live only in the current objective process. The inherited unlabeled artifact and neural weights stay frozen, the current pool is generated de novo rather than retrieved, and bounded numerical fallback uses only its already validated molecules. The protocol supplies batching and execution resources; this intent changes none of them.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a bidirectional masked denoiser on unlabeled molecular fragment sequences and freezes its neural weights. For each objective it ranks previously scored whole molecules, samples high-ranked ones as contexts, and replaces one fragment with a variable-length masked span. The model fills that span while retaining the surrounding fragments and attachment labels. Valid, connected, canonical new molecules are submitted in generation order; accepted scores update the archive and therefore the contexts used next. Parallel denoising usually produces more usable completions than fit in the announced batch, and the Parent discards that surplus.
approach.novelty: Add one mechanism: posterior-sampling selection among the fresh completions already produced by the Parent. A molecular-fingerprint Gaussian process fitted only to accepted scores represents uncertain objective values, and joint posterior draws select distinct completions for the batch. This is the first selector Child in this lineage; its only supplied sibling is the unmodified remasking root. The related graph-evolution experiment made a much larger offspring pool. Here the new selector uses the natural surplus of the existing denoising calls, so the experiment asks whether better use of those alternatives changes the search's best outcomes.

research_intent.falsifier: The intended selector is refuted if completed nondegenerate surplus opportunities never change the submitted generation-order set, if nonfallback choices fail to equal the available-set joint-draw maxima, if samples omit the GP's cross-candidate covariance, or if posterior uncertainty never changes a choice relative to the same-pool posterior-mean maximizer despite eligible nondegenerate opportunities. The accepted-feedback component is refuted by training on unaccepted/future/cross-objective scores or by zero posterior mean and variance response after accepted feedback despite later fit opportunities. Corpus retrieval, changing the denoiser or its proposal distributions, or emitting molecules without inherited context-preserving denoiser provenance would contradict the bound mechanism. Exclusive numerical fallback demonstrates no selector activation. Missing receipts or a run without surplus/uncertainty opportunities make the relevant conclusion inconclusive. Correct conditioning and redirected submissions with flat or worse final scores are negative efficacy evidence, not an execution falsifier; a lower context-beating rate alone also does not refute this selector.

Build a transient ordered pool containing the first occurrence of every connected, context-preserving canonical novel completion from the Parent's existing generation calls.
